title: A dizzy spell in the five-and-ten a week earlier
summary: Marge recalls Zutty nearly fainted buying wrapping paper at the five-and-ten a week before, which they put down to heat; the cause was hypertension they didn't know he had.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: But the week before Zutty went over to the 5 and 10 to get some wrapping paper and cards. We had had a big slab of bacon sent to us Smithfield bacon from Virginia. And we couldn't eat it all so we sent half of it to my sister's. And Zutty said, well send it to Sis, half of it. He went to get the paper and all to wrap it up and he came home and he told me, he said, Marge you know, said, I felt like I was going to fall down. I felt like I was going to faint in the 5 and 10. He said, I had to come outside to get some air.
So I said, I guess it was so hot in there and all. He said, I don't know he said, but I really felt like I was going to faint. We didn't pay any attention to it.
Yes, yes. Because you've really been in very good health.
That's what happened a few days before.
Yes, that's what I said. Before Christmas. It was about a week before when you,

on a Wednesday or something when you came home and told me, said that I almost fell down in the 5 and 10. Said, I got so dizzy and I had to come outside to get some air. I said, well I suppose guess it was just so hot in the 5 and 10.
And it was this hypertension that we didn't know he had.
